root_idea.summary: The root centers on attaching oneself to something or someone for refuge, protection, and concealment.
root_idea.development: From seeking refuge and concealment, the lexical field extends to reciprocal sheltering, circling or encompassing, circumvention, and the side or circuit around a mountain.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form is a distinct Form III verbal noun, normalized from the inflected QAC lemma لِوَاذًا to the citation form لِوَاذٌ.

senses.definition: Reciprocal seeking of refuge or protection by concealing oneself with or behind others; taking shelter and slipping away one after another.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction presents people seeking refuge or concealment in one another. The form is explicitly treated as the verbal noun of لاوذ, rather than the Form I verbal noun لِيَاذٌ.

senses.definition: Evasion: eluding, shunning, or avoiding someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: An attested interpretation of لِوَاذًا in the Quranic passage; this sense emphasizes getting away or avoiding rather than taking shelter.

senses.definition: Acting contrary to, differing from, or being adverse to someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-attested interpretation of the form, with the surrounding passage taken to clarify opposition or noncompliance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have recourse to, seek refuge or protection in, or join oneself to someone or something; to seek aid from it or him and protect oneself by it or him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Commonly constructed with بِـ; the object may be a person, place, or thing serving as refuge, protection, concealment, or support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surround or encompass; to reach or extend to.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A spatial construction describing one place or thing as encircling or reaching another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive to overcome people by maneuvering or employing various means.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِـ in the reported construction لَاذَ بِالقَوْمِ or لَاذَ بِهِمْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go around or encompass people; to surround them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction describing movement around or encirclement of others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To circumvent, delude, wheedle, or beguile someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive interpersonal use involving maneuvering or manipulation; distinct from the Quranic interpretation of evading or shunning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause another to seek refuge or protection in someone or something; alternatively, to protect or conceal another by means of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use relating to refuge, concealment, defense, or fortification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a tropical expression, to cover or conceal the shade with the foot, indicating the arrival of the midday heat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized tropical usage in the expression describing a she-camel covering the shade with her foot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The side, lateral part, or circuit of a mountain; by extension, a side or lateral tract of a region or thing, or a bend in a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A spatial noun; its plural is أَلْوَاذٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A position at the side of, adjacent to, or near a place or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in locative expressions such as being بِـلَوْذِ a place or thing, or being لَوْذَهُ.
A derived abstract noun synonymous with مُرَاوَغَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of refuge, protection, preservation, or concealment; a refuge, fortress, fortified place, or castle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal designation for a place to which one resorts for safety or shelter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression خَيْرٌ مُلَاوِذٌ, little good, or good that comes only after severe toil or difficulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic, marked usage occurring in the fixed expression خَيْرُ بَنِي فُلَانٍ مُلَاوِذٌ.

cautions: The Quranic لِوَاذًا is explicitly analyzed as the Form III verbal noun of لاوذ, not the Form I verbal noun لِيَاذًا.

The single Quran occurrence has multiple attested lexical interpretations: reciprocal sheltering or concealment, evasion, and opposition; the contextual gloss supplied here illustrates the sheltering interpretation.
